contents.name: Section 1: the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra H^Λ_d, the generic isomorphism with the nondegenerate algebra and the contrast between the root-of-unity and degenerate settings

contents.reason: The wedge-tensor Fock module, its column monomial basis and the standard monomial basis are scaffolded on the in-run level-6 page parabolic-category-o-and-fock-space-bases; this page consumes that interface rather than rebuilding it.

contents.name: Sections 2.3-2.4: dual-canonical basis, crystal graph and the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig transition polynomials (2.18)
contents.reason: The dual-canonical/canonical/quasi-canonical Fock families and the parabolic KL transition matrix are scaffolded on the in-run level-6 page; this page only reads the coefficient matrix d_{A,B}(1) from it.

contents.name: Sections 2.5-2.6: reverse tableaux, canonical and quasi-canonical bases, the pairings (2.38)-(2.45)
contents.reason: The four Fock families and their pairings are owned by the level-6 page of this run; the present page imports the transition and pairing identities as its declared suppliers.

contents.name: Theorem 2.7: the normalization P_A = q^{(2Λ-α,α)/2} T_{A↑} of the quasi-canonical family on the highest constituent
Sections 2.7-2.8: multipartition dictionary, integral forms and the specialization at q=1
Section 3.1: parabolic category O, BGG/Arkhipov-Soergel reciprocity and Theorem 3.1
contents.reason: The parabolic category-O categorification of the integral Fock module is scaffolded on the level-6 page of this run; the present page transfers it across the Schur functor.

contents.name: Section 3.2 (3.7)-(3.11): the cyclotomic quotient H^m_d, its PBW dimension l^d·d!, weight idempotents and formal characters
contents.reason: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra itself is the subject of the in-run level-7 page arakawa-suzuki-functors-and-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality; this page only assembles its blocks into a tower.

contents.name: Section 3.2 (3.12)-(3.14): block idempotents e_α and the locally unital tower H^Λ
Section 3.3 (3.15)-(3.20): Grothendieck groups, Cartan pairing, induction/restriction functors and duality
Section 3.4 (3.21)-(3.26): Specht modules via evaluation and induction products, and their duality
contents.reason: The intrinsic Specht modules and their images under the Schur functor are scaffolded on the in-run level-7 page; the decomposition-number theorem here consumes that image statement.

contents.name: Section 3.5 (3.27)-(3.31): Schur-Weyl duality for level l, Theorems 3.6-3.7
contents.reason: The projective generator T^Λ, its endomorphism algebra and the Schur functors are scaffolded on the in-run level-7 page; this page uses them as its transfer mechanism.

contents.name: Section 3.6: Theorem 3.8 (classification of irreducible H^Λ-modules) and Theorem 3.10 (the categorification theorem)
Section 3.6, Theorem 3.10(i)-(iv): the two Grothendieck identifications, the Cartan/Shapovalov comparison and the extension map
Section 3.6, Theorem 3.10(ii)-(iii): standard classes are standard monomials, [S(B)] = Σ_A d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]
Section 3.6, Theorem 3.10(vi): the crystal rule for e_i and f_i on simple modules
Section 3.7: tensoring with sign, transpose of multipartitions and Theorem 3.14
Sections 4.1-4.2: Schur functors commute with duality; Young modules, the double centralizer and the Koszul grading (Corollary 4.8)
contents.reason: No Koszul grading, Ext algebra or graded lift is claimed by this ungraded categorification page; the graded structure is reserved for the separate Hecke/KLR track and is not consumed by any item here.

contents.name: Sections 4.3-4.4: tilting modules, Arkhipov's twisting functor, signed Young modules and Ringel duality (Lemma 4.10, Theorems 4.15 and 4.17, Corollaries 4.18-4.19)

contents.name: Section 1, Main Theorem: blocks of cyclotomic Hecke algebras are sign-modified cyclotomic KLR algebras of type A_∞ (e=0) or A^{(1)}_{e-1} (e>0)

Section 1, Corollary 1: the unique Z-grading with deg y_r = 2 and deg ψ_r e(i) = -a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}
contents.reason: The grading is a strictly finer structure than the ungraded categorification recorded here; no graded decomposition number or Koszul lift is stated on this page, so the corollary is not consumed.

contents.name: Section 6: comparison of blocks at a primitive p-th root of unity with blocks of degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras in characteristic p
contents.reason: This page works over the complex field in characteristic zero and claims no modular or characteristic-p decomposition theory; the comparison is a separate application of the KLR isomorphism.
